key_insight: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) safely visualized intestinal blood-flow biomarkers in children and detected a clear post-meal increase in bowel microvascular perfusion without changing oxygenation.
clinical_relevance: This suggests PAI could become a noninvasive bedside tool for monitoring intestinal vascular health and potentially improving early detection of conditions like necrotizing enterocolitis.
method: 18 healthy pediatric participants were scanned under IRB approval
PAI was performed in all abdominal quadrants before and after a lipid-rich snack
Researchers measured Hb, HbO2, HbT, and sO2 in manually drawn intestinal regions of interest
evidence_signal: The study reported minor, temporary adverse events only and found significant post-prandial hyperemia with no change in bowel oxygen saturation across age cohorts and abdominal regions.
watch_item: Findings come from a small, healthy pediatric sample, so performance in sick infants with suspected NEC still needs validation.
paper_title: Photoacoustic imaging of intestinal physiological biomarkers in infants and children
